title.value: DON’T FLATTEN, TOKENIZE! UNLOCKING THE KEY TO SOFT MOE’S EFFICACY IN DEEP RL
title.justification: The title captures the essence of the research, which emphasizes the novel finding that tokenizing the encoder output is crucial for the efficacy of SoftMixture of Experts (SoftMoEs) in reinforcement learning.
title.quote: DON’T FLATTEN, TOKENIZE! UNLOCKING THE KEY TO SOFT MOE’S EFFICACY IN DEEP RL

analysis.description: This paper provides an in-depth analysis of why SoftMoEs (Soft Mixtures of Experts) are effective in deep reinforcement learning. It uncovers that tokenizing the encoder's output rather than relying on multiple experts is crucial for performance gains, effectively maintaining these gains even with a single expert.

type.justification: The paper includes experimental analyses and results to identify and confirm the factors contributing to the efficacy of SoftMoEs in reinforcement learning.
type.quote: We conduct a series of analyses to identify the key factors that allow soft Mixture of Experts (SoftMoEs) to effectively scale RL agents.

name.justification: The research focuses on using and understanding the architecture of SoftMixtures of Experts within the context of deep reinforcement learning.
name.quote: The use of deep neural networks in reinforcement learning (RL) often suffers from performance degradation as model size increases.

name.justification: The paper specifically investigates the architecture and effectiveness of Mixtures of Experts and their adaptation known as SoftMixtures of Experts.
name.quote: We seek to better understand the true underlying causes for the effectiveness of SoftMoEs in RL settings.

name.justification: A significant focus of the paper is the tokenization process of the encoder output, which is found to be a key factor in the performance gains.
name.quote: We discover the surprising result that tokenizing the encoder output, rather than the use of multiple experts, is what is behind the efficacy of SoftMoEs.

name.justification: Rainbow is referenced as a baseline and as part of the experimental setup to test the efficacy of SoftMoEs.
name.quote: We evaluate performance on the same 20 games of the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE) benchmark used by Obando Ceron* et al. (2024) for direct comparison, with 5 independent seeds for each experiment.

is_contributed.justification: The model is used for evaluation and comparison purposes, not as a new contribution of this research paper.
is_contributed.quote: We mainly focus on the more recent ResNet encoder, but also include some results using the original DQN encoder.

is_executed.justification: The model is part of the experimental setup and results are reported based on its execution.
is_executed.quote: We evaluate performance on the same 20 games of the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE) benchmark used by Obando Ceron* et al. (2024) for direct comparison, with 5 independent seeds for each experiment.

is_compared.justification: Rainbow's performance is compared to other setups including the use of SoftMoEs, showing its role as a baseline for comparison.
is_compared.quote: We perform a careful and thorough investigation into the many parts that make up SoftMoEs aiming to isolate the impact of each.

name.justification: SoftMixture of Experts (SoftMoE) is central to the paper's investigation, which aims to understand its effectiveness in deep reinforcement learning.

is_executed.quote: The genesis of our work is to provide a deeper understanding of SoftMoEs in online RL. For this reason, we will mostly focus on SoftMoEs applied to the Rainbow agent.
